views.name: player_max_overall_rating
views.body_sql:
SELECT MAX(overall_rating) AS max_overall_rating
FROM Player_Attributes
views.description: For each dataset, the maximum overall_rating value across all players (can be joined back to players to find those with that rating).

provenance.question: Which player has the highest overall rating? Indicate the player's api id.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the player (api id) whose overall_rating equals the maximum overall_rating value in the dataset.
Required outputs: api id of the player whose overall_rating is MAX(overall_rating)
Filters: overall_rating = MAX(overall_rating)

tests.purpose: View returns exactly one row (scalar) — detect if view returns 0 or more than 1 rows
tests.sql: SELECT ABS((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_max_overall_rating) - 1)

tests.purpose: max_overall_rating is equal to the MAX(overall_rating) computed from the base table (measure reconciliation)
tests.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN (SELECT max_overall_rating FROM player_max_overall_rating) IS (SELECT MAX(overall_rating) FROM Player_Attributes) THEN 0 ELSE 1 END

tests.purpose: max_overall_rating is not NULL (since MAX over any non-empty numeric column should be NULL only if there are no rows or all NULLs)
tests.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN (SELECT max_overall_rating FROM player_max_overall_rating) IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END

views.name: league_match_goal_totals_by_season
views.body_sql:
SELECT L.id AS league_id, L.name AS league_name, M.season AS season, SUM(M.home_team_goal + M.away_team_goal) AS total_goals
FROM Match M
JOIN League L ON M.league_id = L.id
GROUP BY L.id, L.name, M.season
views.description: Per-league total goals per season computed as the sum of home and away goals across all matches in that league and season (one row per league-season).

provenance.question: Which league had the most goals in the 2016 season?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the league (competition) whose matches in the 2015/2016 season had the highest total number of goals, where total goals for a league equals the sum over all its matches of (home_team_goal + away_team_goal).
Required outputs: league (identifier/name of the competition); total_goals (numeric sum of home_team_goal + away_team_goal across all matches in that league for the specified season)
Filters: season = '2015/2016'; only include matches from that season; aggregate matches by league/competition before comparing totals
Sort/limit: order by total_goals desc limit 1

tests.purpose: View has one row per league-season (no duplicate league_id, league_name, season)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT league_id, league_name, season, COUNT(*) AS c FROM league_match_goal_totals_by_season GROUP BY league_id, league_name, season HAVING c > 1)

tests.purpose: total_goals equals sum of home_team_goal + away_team_goal from Match for that league and season
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM league_match_goal_totals_by_season v LEFT JOIN (SELECT M.league_id AS league_id, L.name AS league_name, M.season AS season, SUM(M.home_team_goal + M.away_team_goal) AS expected_total FROM Match M JOIN League L ON M.league_id = L.id GROUP BY M.league_id, L.name, M.season) s ON v.league_id = s.league_id AND v.league_name = s.league_name AND v.season = s.season WHERE (s.expected_total IS NULL AND (v.total_goals IS NOT NULL)) OR (s.expected_total IS NOT NULL AND v.total_goals IS NULL) OR (s.expected_total IS NOT NULL AND v.total_goals <> s.expected_total)

tests.purpose: Keys league_id, league_name, season are NOT NULL
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM league_match_goal_totals_by_season WHERE league_id IS NULL OR league_name IS NULL OR season IS NULL

views.name: home_match_loss_counts_by_team_and_season
views.body_sql: SELECT m.season, t.team_api_id AS team_api_id, t.team_long_name AS team_long_name, COUNT(m.id) AS home_losses FROM Match m JOIN Team t ON m.home_team_api_id = t.team_api_id WHERE (m.home_team_goal - m.away_team_goal) < 0 GROUP BY m.season, t.team_api_id, t.team_long_name
views.description: Per-team counts of home-match losses (matches where home_team_goal - away_team_goal < 0) for each season, keyed by team identifier and season

provenance.question: Which home team had lost the fewest matches in the 2016 season?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the home team (team name) that had the fewest number of home match losses during the 2015/2016 season, where a home match loss is defined as matches in that season with (home_team_goal - away_team_goal) < 0.
Required outputs: home_team (the name or identifier of the team that played at home); home_losses (the integer count of matches in the 2015/2016 season where home_team_goal - away_team_goal < 0 for that home_team)
Filters: season = '2015/2016'; consider only matches where (home_team_goal - away_team_goal) < 0 when counting losses; group counts by home_team
Sort/limit: order results by home_losses ascending and return the top 1 (the home_team with the minimum home_losses); if multiple teams tie, return all tied teams (no further tie-breaker)

tests.purpose: Each row's home_losses equals the count of Match rows in that season where that team was the home team and lost (home_team_goal - away_team_goal < 0). Detects aggregation or join errors.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT v.season AS season, v.team_api_id AS team_api_id, v.home_losses AS reported, COALESCE(calculated.cnt,0) AS expected FROM home_match_loss_counts_by_team_and_season v LEFT JOIN (SELECT m.season AS season, m.home_team_api_id AS team_api_id, COUNT(m.id) AS cnt FROM "Match" m WHERE (m.home_team_goal - m.away_team_goal) < 0 GROUP BY m.season, m.home_team_api_id) calculated ON calculated.season = v.season AND calculated.team_api_id = v.team_api_id WHERE reported != expected) as _violations

tests.purpose: No NULLs in key columns (season, team_api_id, team_long_name).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM home_match_loss_counts_by_team_and_season WHERE season IS NULL OR team_api_id IS NULL OR team_long_name IS NULL

tests.purpose: View contains no duplicate keys (season, team_api_id, team_long_name) — ensures grain is respected.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT season, team_api_id, team_long_name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM home_match_loss_counts_by_team_and_season GROUP BY season, team_api_id, team_long_name HAVING cnt > 1) as dup

views.name: away_team_season_league_win_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.league_id,
  m.season,
  m.away_team_api_id,
  COUNT(*) AS away_wins_count
FROM Match m
WHERE (m.away_team_goal - m.home_team_goal) > 0
GROUP BY m.league_id, m.season, m.away_team_api_id
views.description: Counts of away match wins per away_team_api_id for each league and season (one row per away team / league / season) where an away win is when away_team_goal > home_team_goal.

provenance.question: In Scotland Premier League, which away team won the most during the 2010 season?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find which away_team_api_id had the most away match wins in matches from the Scotland Premier League during the 2009/2010 season.
Required outputs: away_team_api_id (the ID of the away team); away_wins_count (the number of away matches that team won in that season and league)
Filters: League.name = 'Scotland Premier League'; season = '2009/2010'; A match counts as an away win when (away_team_goal - home_team_goal) > 0
Sort/limit: order by away_wins_count DESC limit 1

tests.purpose: Grain uniqueness: ensure there are no duplicate rows for the declared grain (league_id, season, away_team_api_id) in the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT league_id, season, away_team_api_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM away_team_season_league_win_counts GROUP BY league_id, season, away_team_api_id HAVING cnt > 1) AS t

tests.purpose: Measure correctness: each view row's away_wins_count equals the number of Match rows for that league/season/away_team where away_team_goal > home_team_goal
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM away_team_season_league_win_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT league_id, season, away_team_api_id, COUNT(*) AS calc_count FROM Match WHERE (away_team_goal - home_team_goal) > 0 GROUP BY league_id, season, away_team_api_id) m ON v.league_id = m.league_id AND v.season = m.season AND v.away_team_api_id = m.away_team_api_id WHERE COALESCE(m.calc_count,0) != COALESCE(v.away_wins_count,0)

tests.purpose: Key not NULL: ensure no nulls in any of the declared key columns (league_id, season, away_team_api_id) in the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM away_team_season_league_win_counts WHERE league_id IS NULL OR season IS NULL OR away_team_api_id IS NULL

views.name: team_max_buildup_play_speed
views.body_sql: SELECT t.team_api_id, t.team_long_name, MAX(ta.buildUpPlaySpeed) AS max_buildUpPlaySpeed FROM Team_Attributes ta JOIN Team t ON ta.team_api_id = t.team_api_id GROUP BY t.team_api_id, t.team_long_name
views.description: Per-team maximum recorded buildUpPlaySpeed, joined to team identifier for reuse in comparisons or ranking tasks.

provenance.question: What are the speed in which attacks are put together of the top 4 teams with the highest build Up Play Speed?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the buildUpPlaySpeed values for the top 4 teams ranked by their maximum buildUpPlaySpeed.
Required outputs: team_name (the team identifier/name); buildUpPlaySpeed (the speed in which attacks are put together)
Filters: Consider each team's maximum buildUpPlaySpeed value (i.e., MAX(buildUpPlaySpeed) per team).; Return only the teams with the four highest MAX(buildUpPlaySpeed) values.
Sort/limit: Order results by buildUpPlaySpeed descending and limit to 4 rows

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (team_api_id, team_long_name)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT team_api_id, team_long_name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM team_max_buildup_play_speed GROUP BY team_api_id, team_long_name HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: max_buildUpPlaySpeed equals MAX(buildUpPlaySpeed) computed from Team_Attributes joined to Team for each team
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT v.team_api_id, v.team_long_name FROM team_max_buildup_play_speed v LEFT JOIN (SELECT t.team_api_id, t.team_long_name, MAX(ta.buildUpPlaySpeed) AS expected_max FROM Team_Attributes ta JOIN Team t ON ta.team_api_id = t.team_api_id GROUP BY t.team_api_id, t.team_long_name) e ON v.team_api_id = e.team_api_id AND v.team_long_name = e.team_long_name WHERE (v.max_buildUpPlaySpeed IS NOT e.expected_max) OR (v.max_buildUpPlaySpeed IS NULL AND e.expected_max IS NOT NULL) OR (v.max_buildUpPlaySpeed IS NOT NULL AND e.expected_max IS NULL))

tests.purpose: Keys are not NULL (team_api_id and team_long_name must be present)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM team_max_buildup_play_speed WHERE team_api_id IS NULL OR team_long_name IS NULL

views.name: matches_per_league
views.body_sql: SELECT L.id AS league_id, L.name AS league_name, COUNT(M.id) AS match_count FROM League L JOIN "Match" M ON M.league_id = L.id GROUP BY L.id, L.name
views.description: For each league, the total number of matches played (count of matches grouped by league), keeping league id and name for joins or display.

provenance.question: Give the name of the league with the highest matches of all time and how many matches were played in the said league.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the league name that has the maximum total number of matches played across all time and report that league's name together with the total number of matches played in that league.
Required outputs: League.name — the name of the league that has the highest count of matches; match_count — the total number of matches played in that league (i.e., COUNT of matches where match.league_id = league.id)
Filters: Consider all matches in the matches table (no date or other filtering unless schema requires); Aggregate matches by league_id to compute COUNT(league_id) per league; Select the league (League.name) whose COUNT(league_id) is equal to the maximum COUNT(league_id) over all leagues
Sort/limit: Order by match_count descending and limit to 1 (return a single league with the highest match count)

tests.purpose: Each row in the view has non-NULL league_id and league_name (keys must not be NULL).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM matches_per_league WHERE league_id IS NULL OR league_name IS NULL

tests.purpose: No duplicate grain rows: there should be at most one row per (league_id, league_name).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT league_id, league_name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM matches_per_league GROUP BY league_id, league_name HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: match_count reconciles with base tables: match_count equals the number of Match rows with that league_id (detect mismatches).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM matches_per_league v LEFT JOIN (SELECT league_id AS l_id, COUNT(id) AS expected_count FROM "Match" GROUP BY league_id) b ON v.league_id = b.l_id WHERE COALESCE(b.expected_count,0) != COALESCE(v.match_count,0)

views.name: players_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS id,
  height AS height,
  birthday AS birthday
FROM Player
WHERE birthday >= '1990-01-01 00:00:00' AND birthday < '1996-01-01 00:00:00'
views.description: Select the set of player rows whose birthday is within the given date range (inclusive lower bound, exclusive upper bound). Keep each player row with id and height.

subgoal.text: Select the set of player rows whose birthday is within the given date range (inclusive lower bound, exclusive upper bound). Keep each player row with id and height.

provenance.question: What is the average height of players born between 1990 and 1995?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Compute the average height of players whose birthday is on or after 1990-01-01 00:00:00 and before 1996-01-01 00:00:00, using average height = DIVIDE(SUM(height), COUNT(id)).
Required outputs: average_height: a single numeric value equal to DIVIDE(SUM(height), COUNT(id)) for the selected players
Filters: birthday >= '1990-01-01 00:00:00'; birthday < '1996-01-01 00:00:00'

tests.purpose: No duplicate ids (view grain is id). Fails if the view contains the same id more than once.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT id, COUNT(*) AS c FROM players_cohort GROUP BY id HAVING c > 1)

tests.purpose: All rows satisfy intrinsic birthday filter (birthday >= '1990-01-01' AND birthday < '1996-01-01'). Fails if any row is outside the inclusive lower / exclusive upper bounds or has NULL birthday.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM players_cohort WHERE NOT (birthday >= '1990-01-01 00:00:00' AND birthday < '1996-01-01 00:00:00')

tests.purpose: Each view row corresponds to an existing Player row with matching id and height (detects accidental modification of values or phantom rows). Fails if any view row has no matching base table row or mis
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM players_cohort pc LEFT JOIN Player p ON pc.id = p.id WHERE p.id IS NULL OR (p.height IS NOT pc.height) OR (pc.birthday IS NOT p.birthday)

views.name: league_total_goals
views.body_sql: SELECT League.id AS league_id, League.name AS league_name, SUM(Match.home_team_goal + Match.away_team_goal) AS total_goals FROM Match JOIN League ON Match.league_id = League.id GROUP BY League.id, League.name HAVING SUM(Match.home_team_goal + Match.away_team_goal) IS NOT NULL
views.description: Total goals scored per league across all matches (sum of home and away goals) with league identifiers for joining.

provenance.question: List the top 5 leagues in ascending order of the number of goals made in all seasons combined.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Compute the total number of goals scored across all seasons for each league (where total goals = SUM(home_team_goal + away_team_goal) aggregated over all matches in all seasons), then list the top 5 leagues with the smallest totals (ascending order of total goals).
Required outputs: league (identifier or name of the league); total_goals (integer equal to the sum over all matches of home_team_goal + away_team_goal for that league across all seasons)
Filters: Include all matches from all seasons (no season or date filtering).; Only include leagues that have at least one match (i.e., sum is computed over existing match records).
Sort/limit: ORDER BY total_goals ASC LIMIT 5

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows per grain (league_id, league_name)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT league_id, league_name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM league_total_goals GROUP BY league_id, league_name HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: total_goals equals sum of home_team_goal + away_team_goal from Match for that league (detect mismatches or NULLs)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM league_total_goals v LEFT JOIN (SELECT league_id AS lid, SUM(home_team_goal + away_team_goal) AS expected_total FROM Match GROUP BY league_id) m ON v.league_id = m.lid WHERE (m.expected_total IS NULL AND v.total_goals IS NOT NULL) OR (m.expected_total IS NOT NULL AND v.total_goals IS NULL) OR (m.expected_total IS NOT NULL AND v.total_goals IS NOT NULL AND v.total_goals != m.expected_total)

tests.purpose: Keys league_id and league_name are not NULL
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM league_total_goals WHERE league_id IS NULL OR league_name IS NULL

views.name: player_rows_sel
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.player_name AS player_name,
  p.player_fifa_api_id AS player_fifa_api_id,
  pa.long_shots AS long_shots,
  pa.id AS id,
  p.id AS player_id,
  pa.player_api_id AS player_api_id
FROM Player p
JOIN Player_Attributes pa
  ON pa.player_api_id = p.player_api_id
WHERE p.player_name = 'Ahmed Samir Farag'
views.description: Select all raw rows for the player(s) matching the player name filter. Keep the player identifier and the long_shots value for each source row.

subgoal.text: Select all raw rows for the player(s) matching the player name filter. Keep the player identifier and the long_shots value for each source row.

provenance.question: Find the average number of long-shot done by Ahmed Samir Farag.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Compute the average number of long_shots for the player with name 'Ahmed Samir Farag', where average is defined as SUM(long_shots) divided by COUNT(player_fifa_api_id).
Required outputs: average_long_shot: numeric value equal to DIVIDE(SUM(long_shots), COUNT(player_fifa_api_id))
Filters: player_name = 'Ahmed Samir Farag' (limit aggregation to rows for this player)

tests.purpose: Every row in the view should have player_name equal to the intrinsic filter 'Ahmed Samir Farag'.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_rows_sel WHERE NOT (player_name = 'Ahmed Samir Farag')

tests.purpose: No NULLs allowed for the view's key 'id'.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_rows_sel WHERE id IS NULL

tests.purpose: Each row in the view must correspond to a source Player_Attributes row joined to a Player with matching player_api_id — detect view rows whose player_api_id and id combination does not exist in the ba
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_rows_sel v LEFT JOIN Player p ON v.player_id = p.id LEFT JOIN Player_Attributes pa ON v.id = pa.id WHERE NOT (p.player_name = 'Ahmed Samir Farag' AND pa.player_api_id = p.player_api_id)

views.name: player_long_shot_by_player_fifa_api_id
views.body_sql: SELECT p.player_fifa_api_id AS player_fifa_api_id, pa.id AS player_attributes_id, pa.player_api_id AS player_api_id, CASE WHEN trim(pa.long_shots) = '' THEN NULL ELSE CAST(pa.long_shots AS INTEGER) END AS long_shots_norm FROM Player p JOIN Player_Attributes pa ON pa.player_api_id = p.player_api_id
views.description: Per-player_fifa_api_id normalized long_shots values (one row per Player_Attributes record) with empty-string treated as NULL and long_shots cast to integer, keeping keys to join to player and attributes.

provenance.question: Find the average number of long-shot done by Ahmed Samir Farag.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Compute the average number of long_shots for the player with name 'Ahmed Samir Farag', where average is defined as SUM(long_shots) divided by COUNT(player_fifa_api_id).
Required outputs: average_long_shot: numeric value equal to DIVIDE(SUM(long_shots), COUNT(player_fifa_api_id))
Filters: player_name = 'Ahmed Samir Farag' (limit aggregation to rows for this player)

tests.purpose: View has one row per Player_Attributes.id (no missing or duplicate player_attributes_id).
tests.sql: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Player_Attributes) - (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT player_attributes_id) FROM player_long_shot_by_player_fifa_api_id)

tests.purpose: Every view row corresponds to an existing Player_Attributes record and the keys are preserved (player_attributes_id matches an id and player_api_id matches that row).
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_long_shot_by_player_fifa_api_id v LEFT JOIN Player_Attributes pa ON v.player_attributes_id = pa.id WHERE pa.id IS NULL OR (v.player_api_id IS NOT NULL AND v.player_api_id != pa.player_api_id)

tests.purpose: long_shots_norm is either NULL when source long_shots is empty/blank or equals CAST(long_shots AS INTEGER) from Player_Attributes.
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_long_shot_by_player_fifa_api_id v JOIN Player_Attributes pa ON v.player_attributes_id = pa.id WHERE NOT ( (trim(pa.long_shots) = '' AND v.long_shots_norm IS NULL) OR (trim(pa.long_shots) != '' AND v.long_shots_norm = CAST(pa.long_shots AS INTEGER)) OR (pa.long_shots IS NULL AND v.long_shots_norm IS NULL) )

views.name: team_avg_chancecreationpassing_by_date_and_dribbling
views.body_sql:
SELECT TA.team_api_id AS team_id, T.team_long_name AS team_long_name, TA.date AS attribute_date, AVG(TA.chanceCreationPassing) AS avg_chanceCreationPassing
FROM Team_Attributes TA
JOIN Team T ON TA.team_api_id = T.team_api_id
GROUP BY TA.team_api_id, T.team_long_name, TA.date
views.description: Per-team average chanceCreationPassing for team attribute records filtered by date range and buildUpPlayDribblingClass, including team identifiers and date of the attribute record to allow joins or further filtering.

provenance.question: For the teams with normal build-up play dribbling class in 2014, List the names of the teams with less than average chance creation passing, in descending order of chance creation passing.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: From the records in 2014 for teams whose buildUpPlayDribblingClass is 'Normal', return the team_long_name values for those teams whose average chanceCreationPassing is less than the overall average chanceCreationPassing, listing them in descending order of their average chanceCreationPassing.
Required outputs: team_long_name; average_chanceCreationPassing
Filters: date >= '2014-01-01 00:00:00' AND date <= '2014-01-31 00:00:00'; buildUpPlayDribblingClass = 'Normal'
Sort/limit: ORDER BY average_chanceCreationPassing DESC

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (team_id, team_long_name, attribute_date)
tests.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (
  SELECT team_id, team_long_name, attribute_date, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM team_avg_chancecreationpassing_by_date_and_dribbling
  GROUP BY team_id, team_long_name, attribute_date
  HAVING cnt > 1
)

tests.purpose: avg_chanceCreationPassing equals AVG(chanceCreationPassing) computed from base tables for the same grouping (detects aggregation or join errors)
tests.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (
  SELECT v.team_id, v.team_long_name, v.attribute_date
  FROM team_avg_chancecreationpassing_by_date_and_dribbling v
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT TA.team_api_id AS team_id, T.team_long_name AS team_long_name, TA.date AS attribute_date, AVG(TA.chanceCreationPassing) AS computed_avg
    FROM Team_Attributes TA
    JOIN Team T ON TA.team_api_id = T.team_api_id
    GROUP BY TA.team_api_id, T.team_long_name, TA.date
  ) b ON v.team_id = b.team_id AND v.team_long_name = b.team_long_name AND v.attribute_date = b.attribute_date
  WHERE b.computed_avg IS NULL OR (ABS(v.avg_chanceCreationPassing - b.computed_avg) > 0.000001)
)

tests.purpose: Keys are not NULL (team_id, team_long_name, attribute_date must be present)
tests.sql:
SELECT (COALESCE(
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM team_avg_chancecreationpassing_by_date_and_dribbling WHERE team_id IS NULL),0) +
  COALESCE((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM team_avg_chancecreationpassing_by_date_and_dribbling WHERE team_long_name IS NULL),0) +
  COALESCE((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM team_avg_chancecreationpassing_by_date_and_dribbling WHERE attribute_date IS NULL),0)
) AS violations

views.name: league_season_home_away_avg_goals

views.description: Per league and season average goals scored by home teams and by away teams (one row per league-season with avg_home_goal and avg_away_goal)

provenance.question: List the name of leagues in which the average goals by the home team is higher than the away team in the 2009/2010 season.

Task: Find the names of leagues for the 2009/2010 season where the average goals scored by the home team is greater than the average goals scored by the away team.
Required outputs: League.name (the league name)
Filters: season = '2009/2010'; AVG(home_team_goal) > AVG(away_team_goal) per league

tests.purpose: View has one row per league_id, league_name, season (no duplicate keys)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT league_id, league_name, season, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM league_season_home_away_avg_goals GROUP BY league_id, league_name, season HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: avg_home_goal and avg_away_goal match averages recomputed from base Match table for the same league and season
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM league_season_home_away_avg_goals v LEFT JOIN (SELECT league_id, season, AVG(home_team_goal) AS exp_avg_home, AVG(away_team_goal) AS exp_avg_away FROM "Match" GROUP BY league_id, season) m ON v.league_id = m.league_id AND v.season = m.season WHERE NOT ((m.exp_avg_home IS NULL AND v.avg_home_goal IS NULL) OR (m.exp_avg_home IS NOT NULL AND ABS(v.avg_home_goal - m.exp_avg_home) < 1e-9)) OR NOT ((m.exp_avg_away IS NULL AND v.avg_away_goal IS NULL) OR (m.exp_avg_away IS NOT NULL AND ABS(v.avg_away_goal - m.exp_avg_away) < 1e-9))

tests.purpose: Keys league_id, league_name, season are never NULL

views.name: players_with_high_vision_from_player_attributes
views.body_sql:
SELECT
    p.id,
    p.player_api_id,
    p.player_name,
    p.player_fifa_api_id,
    pa.id AS player_attributes_id,
    pa.date,
    pa.vision
FROM
    Player p
JOIN
    Player_Attributes pa
    ON pa.player_api_id = p.player_api_id
WHERE
    pa.vision > 89

params.description: Each row represents a Player joined to one of their Player_Attributes records where that attributes record has vision > 89; columns are player fields from Player and the linked Player_Attributes id, date, and vision.
params.when_to_use: To get all Player_Attributes records (and basic Player info) for players whose specific attributes record has a very high vision score (>89). | As a starting set when you need player identity (id, player_api_id, player_name, player_fifa_api_id) together with the attributes record id, date, and vision for high-vision attribute snapshots. | When joining to other tables keyed by Player.id or Player_Attributes.id for analyses focused on these attribute rows.
params.when_not_to_use: When you need one row per player regardless of how many high-vision attribute records they have — the view keeps one row per Player_Attributes record (grain = player_attributes_id), so players with multiple qualifying records appear multiple times. | When you need the latest (or earliest) attribute record per player — the view does not filter or aggregate by date, so it does not enforce any time-window or selection of a single snapshot. | When you need players who never have vision >89 — those players are excluded by the WHERE filter on pa.vision. | When you expect attributes joined by player_fifa_api_id instead of player_api_id — the join path is specifically ON pa.player_api_id = p.player_api_id and would miss matches that only align on player_fifa_api_id. | When you need aggregated statistics (counts, averages, max/min) across attribute records — this view exposes raw rows with no aggregation. | When you need a different vision threshold or a range — the intrinsic filter pa.vision > 89 is hard-coded and will produce incomplete results for other thresholds or inclusive bounds.
